title: Pt-induced semimetallic transport and enhanced thermoelectric response in the half-Heusler alloy YNi_{0.5}Pt_{0.5}Bi
authors: Vikas Chahar, Shivam Rathod, Lankun Wang, Sneh, Shubhadeep Bej, Divya Prakash Dubey, Dinesh Dixit, Abdelmoneim Elkhouly, Raúl Cardoso-Gil, Zihang Liu, Xiao Xu, Rie Y. Umetsu, Ratnamala Chatterjee, Kaustuv Manna
abstract: Half-Heusler alloys provide a versatile platform for tuning electronic and thermal transport through chemical substitution. Here, we investigate the thermoelectric and magnetotransport properties of spark-plasma-sintered YNi_{0.5}Pt_{0.5}Bi. Partial substitution of Ni by Pt drives YNiBi toward semimetallic transport, characterized by hole-dominated conduction, a low Hall carrier concentration of $\mathrm{1.9 \times 10^{19} cm^{-3}}$, and a sizeable nonsaturating magnetoresistance of 18$\%$ at 300 K under 14 T. Compared with YNiBi, Pt alloying increases the room-temperature Seebeck coefficient from approximately 90 to 130 $\mathrm{μV K^{-1}}$, while reducing the thermal conductivity to 3.15 $\mathrm{W m^{-1} K^{-1}}$. Single-parabolic-band analysis indicates an enhanced carrier effective mass, resulting in a room-temperature power factor of 13.7 $\mathrm{μW cm^{-1} K^{-2}}$ and a figure of merit ($zT$= 0.13). First-principles calculations further show a Pt-induced closing of the electronic band gap and a low density of states near the Fermi level, consistent with the experimentally observed semimetal-like transport. These results demonstrate that Ni/Pt alloying provides an effective route for simultaneously tuning the electronic, magnetotransport, and thermoelectric properties of YNiBi-based half-Heusler compounds.
summary: This paper demonstrates that partially substituting Ni with Pt in the half-Heusler alloy YNiBi creates a semimetallic material with superior thermoelectric performance. By simultaneously tuning electronic and thermal properties, the alloying approach offers an effective pathway for developing high-performance thermoelectric materials.
main_problem: The study investigates how substituting Ni with Pt in the half-Heusler alloy YNiBi tunes its electronic, magnetotransport, and thermoelectric properties.
main_result: Pt alloying drives the material toward semimetallic transport, significantly enhancing the Seebeck coefficient and achieving a figure of merit ($zT$) of 0.13 at room temperature.
method: The research combines experimental measurements (magnetotransport, thermoelectric characterization) with first-principles calculations (DFT) to analyze the electronic structure.
model_or_system: The physical system is the half-Heusler alloy $	ext{YNi}_{0.5}	ext{Pt}_{0.5}	ext{Bi}$, which is synthesized via spark-plasma-sintering. Theoretical analysis uses DFT to model band structure changes.
key_observables: Seebeck coefficient, thermal conductivity ($\kappa$), power factor ($	ext{PF}$), figure of merit ($zT$), magnetoresistance ($	ext{MR}$), and electronic band gap.
important_parameters: Room temperature (300 K), applied magnetic field (14 T), and the alloying ratio ($	ext{Ni}/	ext{Pt}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on single-parabolic-band approximations and the use of established transport models like the Wiedemann-Franz law.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the paper analyzes multiple transport properties (Resistivity vs. T, MR vs. B, S vs. T) and compares results to theoretical predictions.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of synthesis/characterization, detailed measurement of transport properties (electrical, thermal, magnetic), and theoretical confirmation of the electronic structure changes.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state thermoelectrics, the concept of tuning electronic band structure (closing the gap) via chemical substitution is relevant to engineering quantum materials for enhanced transport phenomena.
